meta.title: Pianissimo
meta.tagline: Vienna, 1928. One wax cylinder holds the last glass-lark call. The floors alarm above a whisper. The quartet starts at eight.
meta.tone: hushed, wry, tender, tense as a held breath
meta.premise: The Museum of Vanished Sound keeps the only recording of the Carniolan glass-lark, a bird that sang in two notes at once and has not been heard alive since 1899. Director Adelheid Stillhart keeps it in a felt-lined vault under parquet floors that ring an alarm at any sound above a whisper. Tonight a string quartet plays the centenary gala in the rotunda. Ottilie Graf, a piano tuner with perfect pitch, has her crew: Mirela the deaf locksmith, Haberl the retired opera prompter, and Herr Kapellmeister, a very calm cat. Under the music, they go in.
meta.prompt: A Viennese museum holds the only recording of an extinct bird's call, locked behind floors that alarm at any sound above a whisper. Assemble a crew — a deaf locksmith, a retired opera prompter and a very calm cat — and lift it during a live string quartet.

str.name: Bearing
str.description: Looking like you belong here. Tailcoat posture, a nod to the usher.

dex.name: Light Feet
dex.description: Moving between creaks. Fingers that do not rattle keys.

int.name: Perfect Pitch
int.description: Hearing the room. Fuels whispered tricks and cues.

hp.name: Composure
hp.description: How long you keep your nerve. At zero you gasp, and the whole museum hears it.

mp.name: Breath
mp.description: Air held in reserve for whispers, cues and long silences.

ac.name: Cover Story
ac.description: How convincingly you are a guest who took a wrong turn.

statuses.name: Flustered
statuses.description: Your ears ring and your feet forget where the quiet boards are.

statuses.name: Slipping on Marbles
statuses.description: Feet skating on rolling glass. Cannot move.

statuses.name: Enraptured
statuses.description: Listening to the music with eyes closed, forgetting why they came.

statuses.name: Hushed
statuses.description: The Director's silence presses on your throat. No whispers, no cues.

statuses.name: Lost in Stage Smoke
statuses.description: A puff of theatre smoke. Nobody can find you in it.

statuses.name: Fed a Line
statuses.description: Mouthing a prompted line, they believe they are meant to be somewhere else.

statuses.name: Csárdás Feet
statuses.description: The tempo got into your legs. Everything goes at double speed.

statuses.name: Purr-warmed
statuses.description: A calm cat purred against your shins. Composure returns, slowly.

statuses.name: On Cue
statuses.description: Haberl's whisper in your ear: every step lands exactly between the beats.

resources.name: Hush
resources.description: How quiet you have been. Every time you are rattled the floor hears it. At zero the parquet sings and the watch comes running.

onEmpty.text: The parquet sings: a long, bright chord from wall to wall. Lanterns swing in the stairwell.

rules.name: Whisper Floors
rules.description: Every time you lose Composure you also lose 1 Hush. At 0 Hush the floor sings: a Night Watchman comes running and your Hush resets to 5.

rules.name: The Quartet Plays On
rules.description: Every 25 turns the quartet swells into a forte. Under the noise you regain 1 Hush and 2 Breath.

player.name: Ottilie Graf
player.title: Piano Tuner, Crew Lead
player.description: Forty years of tuning the pianos of Vienna's best salons. She can hear a loose floorboard three rooms away and knows exactly which ones the Director never fixed.

perks.name: Steady Hands
perks.description: Your fingers stop shaking. +1 Light Feet.

perks.name: Singer's Lungs
perks.description: Haberl taught you to breathe like a mezzo. +4 Breath.

perks.name: The Prompter's Trick
perks.description: Learn Feed a Line: whisper a cue and someone wanders off to deliver it.

perks.name: Airtight Cover Story
perks.description: You really are the Director's niece. +1 Cover Story, +1 Bearing.

perks.name: Sing It Back
perks.description: Learn Sing It Back: hum a note so exact that everything nearby rings and reels.

perks.name: Soft Soles
perks.description: Half the time you are rattled, the floor does not notice: regain the Hush you would lose.

perks.name: Interval Bar
perks.description: When Composure runs low, you remember the champagne at the interval and recover 8.

perks.name: Inner Applause
perks.description: Each time you outfox someone, a little applause in your head steadies you: recover 3 Composure.

perks.name: Absolute Ear
perks.description: You hear guards before they see you. +2 Perfect Pitch, +1 sight.

actors.name: Night Docent
actors.description: A volunteer in lavender wool who has shushed three emperors' grandchildren and fears nothing but crumbs.

actors.name: Loose Parquet
actors.description: A herringbone board that has been waiting decades to creak at exactly the wrong moment.

actors.name: Listening Horn
actors.description: A brass ear-trumpet on a stand, wired to the Director's office. It swivels toward breathing.

actors.name: Night Watchman
actors.description: Brass buttons, a hooded lantern and orders to bring anyone who whispers to the Director.

actors.name: Echo Moth
actors.description: Pale moths bred in the sound archive. They eat silence and repeat your footsteps, louder.

actors.name: Restless Specimen
actors.description: A stuffed capercaillie on a walnut plinth. Its glass eyes follow you; when you get close, it hops down to look closer.

actors.name: Stray Semiquaver
actors.description: A sixteenth note that fell out of the second violin's part and now hunts for anything to land on.

actors.name: The Wolf Tone
actors.description: Every cello has one note that howls. Tonight the cellist's escaped into the music and it is hungry.

actors.name: Metronome Sentry
actors.description: A walnut metronome the height of a child, ticking at exactly 60. It stops only to listen.

actors.name: Hofrätin Adelheid Stillhart
actors.description: Director of the Museum of Vanished Sound. She has not raised her voice since 1899, and she has never needed to.

abilities.name: Call the Watch
abilities.description: She lifts one gloved finger. Lantern light in the corridor.

abilities.name: Absolute Quiet
abilities.description: A look that takes the breath out of your throat.

npc.personality: Precise, dry, wounded. Speaks in a near-whisper and expects the room to lean in. Loves the glass-lark more than any living person.
npc.greeting: Frau Graf. You tuned my mother's Bösendorfer. You were the only one who never let the A drift. Why are you standing on my floor?
lines: Sound is a thing that ends. I make it stop ending.
If it is played, it is spent. I will not spend the last of anything.
The quartet is very good tonight. Nobody will hear you scream politely.
npc.secrets: She was on the 1899 expedition that recorded the lark. She sold the location of the last nesting cliff to a collector for the funds to build this vault. She has never played the cylinder.
npc.wants: To be forgiven without ever being asked. To keep the cylinder silent forever.

actors.name: Mirela Kovač
actors.description: Deaf since childhood, she feels tumblers through her fingertips and reads lips across a ballroom. She thinks this job is funny.

npc.personality: Dry, quick, signs faster than anyone can talk. Unbothered by alarms she cannot hear; deeply bothered by bad locks.
npc.greeting: (She signs, then mouths slowly) You're late. I brought the good picks. Kreuzer first, sentiment later.
lines: The vault lock is a Kromer with a felt-damped bolt. Beautiful. I'm almost sorry.
Watch the floor, not the guards. Guards blink. The floor never does.
If the cat sits down, stop. The cat knows.
npc.secrets: She cut a copy of the Director's office key in 1925 for a different job that fell through. She has no idea it still works.
npc.wants: To open the Kromer vault lock once, just to know she can. Payment in cash, not in feelings.

actors.name: Ferdinand Haberl
actors.description: Forty-one seasons in the prompter's box of the Court Opera. He has been hiding in a display case labelled 'Viennese Gentleman, c. 1880' since noon.

npc.personality: Theatrical, kind, whispers everything as if from under a stage. Knows the quartet's score by heart and times the heist by it.
npc.greeting: Psst. Up here. No, here. Second movement begins in four minutes; the fortissimo is bar ninety. Did you bring my cue sheet? I dropped it near the grouse.
lines: When in doubt, wait for the forte. Every footstep is free under a forte.
The cellist is ours. Zsófia. Her grandfather recorded the lark.
Never step on a board with a knot like an eye. I have opinions about that board.
npc.secrets: The quartet's encore is the glass-lark's call transcribed for strings by the cellist. When it plays, every ear in the building turns to the rotunda, including the Director's.
npc.wants: One last perfect cue. To hear the lark, once, before he goes properly deaf himself.

actors.name: Zsófia Erdős
actors.description: The quartet's cellist, somehow also standing here inside her own second movement, bow in hand, perfectly unsurprised to see you.

npc.personality: Calm, wry, intensely focused; talks in tempo markings. Her grandfather recorded the lark and she wants it to sing again.
npc.greeting: Keep to the held notes; they hold your weight. The rests do not. And mind my wolf tone, it bites.
lines: My grandfather wrote the lark's call down in two staves. Two notes at once. I spent nine years learning to bow it.
The encore is the lark. When Haberl gives the cue, I play it, and the whole museum forgets to breathe.
Stillhart was on that expedition too. Ask her who bought the cliff.
npc.secrets: Her grandfather and the Director were engaged in 1899. The Director sold the nesting cliff; he never spoke to her again.
npc.wants: For the recording to be played aloud, once, in a full hall.

actors.name: Herr Kapellmeister
actors.description: A very calm ginger cat. He weighs exactly enough not to trip the pressure plates and he has never once been in a hurry.

npc.personality: Utterly calm. Blinks slowly. Purrs at the pitch of a well-tuned A. Responds to nothing and everything.
npc.greeting: (Herr Kapellmeister looks at you. He blinks, very slowly. Somehow, everything is fine.)
lines: (He settles onto the pressure plate beside the plinth. It does not make a sound.)
(A purr, at exactly 440 hertz. Your heartbeat slows to match it.)
(He looks at the Director, then at you, then washes one paw.)
npc.secrets: The cat has been sitting in this vault every night for a week. The Director feeds him sardines and talks to him about 1899.
npc.wants: Sardines. A warm lap. For nobody to run.

items.name: A-440 Tuning Fork
items.description: Steel, warm from your pocket. Struck against a knee, it hums a note so pure that people turn to find it.

items.name: Conductor's Baton
items.description: White birch with a cork grip, dropped by someone who conducted this very movement once.
items.vagueText: It seems to want to be pointed at someone. People tend to obey where it points.

items.name: Rented Tailcoat
items.description: From Lanner and Sons, Mariahilfer Straße. A gala guest's armour: nobody questions a tailcoat.

items.name: Felt Overshoes
items.description: Grey felt galoshes from a church sexton. They make a person very hard to hear and slightly hard to take seriously.
items.vagueText: Soft, thick, silent. Worn over shoes, they seem to make you harder to catch.

items.name: Mother-of-Pearl Opera Glasses
items.description: For spotting rivals across a dress circle. Equally good for spotting watchmen across a gallery.

items.name: Brass Violin Mute
items.description: A little comb of brass that clips onto a bridge to soften a violin.
items.vagueText: Clipped to anything, it makes it quieter. Perhaps that includes you.

items.name: Slice of Sachertorte
items.description: Wrapped in wax paper, apricot under the chocolate. One bite and the world is briefly reasonable.

items.name: Valerian Drops
items.description: A brown bottle from the Engel-Apotheke. Twelve drops on the tongue and the shakes go away.

items.name: Hush Pastille
items.description: Throat lozenges in a mint-green tin. Suck one and you stop rustling, sniffing and swallowing for a while.

items.name: Cake of Rosin
items.description: Amber violin rosin. You hold it under your nose: pine, dust, concert halls. You breathe deeper.

items.name: Bag of Marbles
items.description: Glass marbles in a velvet pouch. Scattered under feet they stop pursuit cold, though not quietly.

items.name: Stage Smoke Pellet
items.description: Haberl's own recipe from Die Zauberflöte, 1902. Crush it and vanish in a soft grey puff.

items.name: Field Notes, Carniola 1899
items.description: A water-stained notebook with a floor plan sketched on the back. Two sets of initials: J.E. and A.S.

effects.text: 'A.S. insists the cliff must stay secret. I agree. We are engaged; I trust her.' Underneath, in other ink: the vault plan, and a note on which boards are loose.

items.name: Haberl's Cue Sheet
items.description: Bar numbers, pencilled in Haberl's tiny hand: every forte of the second movement, and the exact bar where you can step into the music.

items.name: The Prompter's Last Cue
items.description: A rolled card with one word in red: 'ENCORE'. Read it aloud at the right moment and the quartet plays the lark.

effects.text: You whisper the cue. Far above, a cello begins two notes at once. Every ear in the building turns toward the rotunda.

items.name: Cylinder No. 7: The Glass-Lark
items.description: Brown wax in a felt-lined brass case, 1899. The only recording of the Carniolan glass-lark. It is lighter than you expected.

items.name: Cylinder: Carinthian Lullaby
items.description: A grandmother singing, close to the horn. You play it against your ear and remember being small.

items.name: Cylinder: Deutschmeister Band March
items.description: A military band at full blast, captured in 1904. Precisely the wrong thing to play here.

items.name: Cylinder: Lecture on Ventilation
items.description: The museum architect, droning through every duct, door and stair of the building in 1911.

items.name: Cylinder: Csárdás at Double Speed
items.description: Somebody wound the phonograph too tight. The fiddle sprints, and your feet sprint after it.

items.name: Feed a Line
items.description: Whisper someone their next line, the way Haberl did for forty seasons. They wander off to deliver it.

items.name: Sing It Back
items.description: Hum a note exactly in tune with the room. Everything nearby rings like a struck glass and forgets what it was doing.

terrains.name: Singing Parquet
terrains.description: Boards tuned by the Director herself. Stand on them and they hum a soft, accusing chord.

terrains.name: Display Case
terrains.description: Glass and walnut. Inside: a songbird nobody will hear again, and a label in copperplate.

effects.text: Behind the specimen, somebody tucked a tin of lozenges and a note: 'For the crew. H.'

terrains.name: Velvet Rope
terrains.description: Brass stanchions and crimson velvet. Stepping over it is slow and undignified.

terrains.name: Held Note
terrains.description: A sustained viola tone, solid as a plank and warm underfoot. Standing on it, you breathe easier.

terrains.name: Felt Wedges
terrains.description: Pyramids of grey felt, floor to ceiling, swallowing every sound in the vault.

cylinders.label: Cylinder wrapped in a love letter

areas.name: The Staff Entrance
areas.description: Back corridors under the museum: cloakrooms, crates of unlabelled cylinders, a porter's lodge with a dead telephone. Gaslight, herringbone parquet, and somewhere above, a quartet tuning.
areas.transitionName: Ride the dumbwaiter up to the galleries
areas.gmNotes: Introduce the crew via Mirela. Upstairs the quartet tunes; the player should feel the floor listening. Watchmen are bored, docents are not.

areas.name: Gallery of Extinct Song
areas.description: Marble halls of glass cases: stuffed songbirds, phonographs, a wall of silent wax cylinders. Every specimen faces the door you came through.
areas.transitionName: Step into the music on Haberl's cue
areas.gmNotes: Haberl hides in a display case labelled 'Viennese Gentleman'. The cue sheet lies near a guarded specimen. The field notes hint that the Director and the cellist's grandfather were engaged.

areas.name: Inside the Second Movement
areas.description: Step through the music and you are standing on it: held notes as golden platforms over a violet dark, bow strokes as bridges, the four instruments booming somewhere below like weather.
areas.transitionName: Fall through the final rest into the vault
areas.gmNotes: Non-realistic space: the music made physical. Footsteps make no noise here except on silence. Zsófia reveals the encore is the lark's call; the Prompter's Last Cue lies far off. The Wolf Tone howls.

areas.name: The Room of Absolute Quiet
areas.description: A round vault lined with felt wedges, so silent you hear your own blood. In the centre, under a glass bell on a plinth, a brass case glows faintly. The Director is already here.
areas.transitionName: Walk out through the gala, cylinder under your coat
areas.gmNotes: The finale. The Director guards the plinth and will talk first. Two routes: outfox her, or use the Prompter's Last Cue so the encore draws every ear away, then take the cylinder. The cat sits on a pressure plate, perfectly calm.

goal.summary: Lift Cylinder No. 7 from the Room of Absolute Quiet: outfox Director Stillhart, or call Haberl's encore so every ear turns to the stage.
goal.winText: You walk out through the rotunda as the encore begins: a cello and a viola playing two notes at once, the glass-lark's call, the first time anyone has heard it in twenty-nine years. In your coat the cylinder is warm. Behind you, very quietly, the Director is weeping. Herr Kapellmeister follows you out, in no hurry at all.
goal.lossText: You gasp. In the Room of Absolute Quiet a gasp is a thunderclap. The parquet sings, the lanterns come, and the glass-lark stays silent for another hundred years.

gm.persona: Haberl's annotated prompt book: the heist written as an opera libretto, the stage directions narrating themselves from the prompter's box.
gm.voice: Short stage directions in the present tense, with tempo markings (pianissimo, attacca, fermata). Warm, wry, never loud.
threads: The floor listens: every creak is a chord the Director tuned herself.
The quartet's encore is the lark's call, transcribed by the cellist.
The Director and the cellist's grandfather were engaged on the 1899 expedition.
Herr Kapellmeister is suspiciously at home in the vault.
Haberl is going deaf and wants to hear the lark once.

fallback.intro: Act One. A service door in the Burgring, eight o'clock. Upstairs a string quartet tunes for the Schubert gala; down here the gaslight ticks. Ottilie Graf, piano tuner, buttons a rented tailcoat. Somewhere above the floors are listening, and somewhere below them, a bird that has been silent since 1899 waits in wax. Pianissimo, please.
areaEnter: Scene one: the staff entrance. Mirela is waiting by the cloakroom, already signing that you are late. Mind the parquet. It was tuned.
Scene two: the gallery. Glass cases, glass eyes. A stuffed grouse turns its head a fraction. One display case labelled 'Viennese Gentleman' winks.
Scene three, attacca: you step into the second movement. The floor is a held note. Below you, a cello breathes.
Finale: the Room of Absolute Quiet. Felt swallows your footsteps. A ginger cat blinks at you from beside the plinth. The Director does not turn around.
lowHp: Your hands are shaking. The floor can hear your hands shaking.
Breathe in four counts, out four. Haberl's voice, from somewhere: 'Not yet. Not yet.'
events: Above, the quartet swells into a forte. For eight bars, nothing you do can be heard.
A lantern swings past a doorway and keeps going.
A moth lands on your sleeve and repeats your heartbeat back to you, louder.
Far off, Haberl coughs exactly on the downbeat, and a guard turns the wrong way.

audio.mood: A string quartet heard through floorboards: hushed pizzicato, long held notes, a metronome ticking somewhere.
searchTerms: Death and the Maiden second movement
suggestions: Schubert: String Quartet No. 14, II. Andante con moto
Haydn: The Lark quartet, I. Allegro moderato
